summary: Port-Menier Airport (YPN) serves Port-Menier, the sole permanent settlement on Anticosti Island, a remote and largely uninhabited landmass in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, Quebec. The airport functions as a critical year-round link for residents, seasonal workers, and visitors, as the island's isolation makes air access essential in addition to the seasonal ferry service from the mainland. Anticosti itself is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, making the airport the gateway to one of Canada's most unspoiled natural environments.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Port-Menier Airport?
A: Air Liaison provides scheduled passenger flights connecting Port-Menier with Sept-Îles on the Quebec mainland, with occasional seasonal service to other regional destinations.

Q: Can I reach Anticosti Island by road?
A: No, Anticosti Island is not connected to the mainland by bridge. Travelers must fly to Port-Menier Airport or take the Relais Nordik ferry from Sept-Îles, which operates on a limited seasonal schedule.

Q: Is Port-Menier Airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates throughout the year, though weather conditions in the Gulf of St. Lawrence can occasionally cause delays or cancellations, particularly in winter.

Q: Are there car rentals available at the airport?
A: Limited vehicle rentals and shuttle services are available in Port-Menier, but it is advisable to arrange transportation in advance given the small size of the community.
transport_tips: There is no public transit system on Anticosti Island, so arranging a rental car, shuttle, or local guide in advance is strongly recommended. The airport terminal is small and only a short drive from Port-Menier village, and most accommodations can be reached within minutes.
